about: The mutant ledger of internal/lawledger: edits of the ledger reader and its statement comparison (Same) that its tests, or Same's licence in internal/sketch/stdlib, must kill. Run it with go run ./scripts/mutants ./internal/lawledger. Seeded by LEDGER-SAME (wf10 std).

mutants.name: same-counts-all-space
mutants.from: func Same(a, b string) bool { return slices.Equal(tokens(a), tokens(b)) }
mutants.to: func Same(a, b string) bool { return Normalize(a) == Normalize(b) }
mutants.rule: A law reformatted with gofmt-style operator spacing states the same law.

mutants.name: same-joins-tokens
mutants.from: func Same(a, b string) bool { return slices.Equal(tokens(a), tokens(b)) }
mutants.to: func Same(a, b string) bool { return strings.Join(tokens(a), "") == strings.Join(tokens(b), "") }
mutants.rule: White space between two words separates tokens: let it is not letit.

mutants.name: same-drops-op-space
mutants.rule: An operator is the scanner's longest: a - -b is not a --b.

mutants.name: same-strips-literals
mutants.rule: White space inside a string literal is the law's text: "a, b" is not "a,b".

mutants.name: same-ends-literal-at-escape
mutants.rule: An escaped quote does not end a literal.

mutants.name: same-paren-in-word
mutants.rule: A parenthesis is a token of its own: ( !x) is (!x), as the formatter prints it.

mutants.name: same-interpolation-as-text
mutants.rule: The code of a string's interpolation is tokens, as the formatter formats it: "\((n%7+7)%7)" is "\((n % 7 + 7) % 7)".

mutants.name: same-licence-skips-plain-law
mutants.from:
fromSource, err := format(src)
		if err != nil {
mutants.to:
fromSource, err := format(src)
		if err != nil || strings.Contains(src, "!") {
mutants.rule: Same's licence skips only the member rewrite laws the formatter cannot take alone; a skip of any other law fails it.

mutants.name: compare-missing-restatement-passes
mutants.rule: A runner restates every law its lines list for it (stdlib.md, Std laws 4).

mutants.name: compare-statement-unchecked
mutants.rule: A runner's statement is held to the law's source text (stdlib.md, Std laws 4).

mutants.name: run-unknown-key-passes
mutants.rule: A law with no source text fails lawledger.Run, naming parsed.Run; it is never skipped.

mutants.name: statement-stops-at-first-brace
mutants.to: if start < 0 || c != '}' || len(stack) != depth && false {
mutants.rule: A law's statement runs to the brace that closes its body, not the first one.

mutants.name: statement-counts-braces-in-strings
mutants.rule: A brace inside a string, raw string or rune literal opens no block.

mutants.name: statement-ignores-the-type
mutants.rule: A member law Type.Law is cut from Type's body, not from the first law of that name.

mutants.name: runners-short-line-read
mutants.rule: A runner-file line is two tab-separated cells, a key and a runner.
